title: Phoenix OmniOps burst capacity proposal & field notes
content:
Executive summary:

This note captures the results of a focused POC we ran with Phoenix OmniOps during the week of 2027-11-08 to evaluate burst behavior, tail latency, and unit cost tradeoffs for a reranking/search use case. The customer traffic pattern is bursty (ad-hoc spikes from batch reindex + user-driven campaigns) with strict p95 SLO of 300ms for the top-tier path. They asked for a recommended Dedicated deployment shape and an operations playbook for handling microbursts up to 6x baseline QPS.

High-level findings:
- Baseline: single-region Dedicated pool (4x A100-80GB) serving redwood-mini-13b (4-bit) without prefix caching yielded steady-state throughput ~220 qps for short prompts (avg input tokens 45) with p95 ~340ms under 1x load.
- Under burst to 4x steady-state QPS, p95 tail increased to 1.2s and p99 > 2.5s due to queuing and KV-cache cold starts across nodes.
- Enabling per-request prefix caching + adaptive batching (max batch 32, latency cap 120ms) recovers p95 to ~380ms at 4x QPS and keeps p99 < 900ms for most bursts.
- Cost: projected hosted-fallback cost when autoscaling to extra capacity is ~3.6x the Dedicated marginal cost per 1M tokens. Quantization (4-bit) + caching reduced effective token cost by ~55% vs 16-bit baseline.

Test environment and configs:
- Model: redwood-mini-13b-4bit (quantized build, identical weights to customer canonical model).
- Hardware (Dedicated): 4 x A100-80GB (DGX-style), node CPU 2x 32-core, 1Gbps interconnect simulated with colocated subnet.
- Fallback (hosted): same model variant on mGPU pool (multi-tenant) scaled as needed.
- Traffic profile: mixture of small interactive queries (75%) avg input 45 tokens, and longer rerank contexts (25%) avg input 220 tokens. Baseline steady-state = 220 qps. Burst tests: 2x, 4x, 6x steady-state injected as sudden step load sustained for 3 minutes then ramp down.
- Serving runtime features toggled: prefix/KV cache (on/off), adaptive batching (on/off) with latency cap 120ms, sequence caching warmup (pre-warm 10K keys), model quantization 4-bit vs 8-bit baseline.
- Metrics collected: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency (inference end-to-end), token/sec, GPU utilization, queue length, cold-start counts, and estimated cost per 1M tokens (based on committed Dedicated rate + hosted fallback rates).

Observed results (selected):
- Steady-state (1x) baseline: qps 220, p50 80ms, p90 180ms, p95 340ms, p99 720ms, GPU util avg 62%.
- Burst 4x without caching/batching: qps peaking 720, p95 1.2s, p99 2.6s, queue depth up to 160 requests, GPU util 98% (saturation).
- Burst 4x with caching + adaptive batching: qps sustained 680, p95 380ms, p99 870ms, queue depth < 40, GPU util 88% (more efficient packed tokens).
- Burst 6x with caching + batching + pre-warm: qps 1320 (with hosted fallback engaged), local Dedicated handled ~5x of baseline (1100 qps) and hosted fallback supplied remaining capacity. Observed cross-pool latency impacts on fallback path: p95 fallback 480ms, combined p95 420ms overall.
- Cold-start contribution: when prefix cache is cold across >50% of nodes, p99 spikes observed around 2.8s; pre-warm (populate cache from sampling run) reduced cold-start spikes by ~75%.

Cost summary (projected per 1M output+input tokens):
- Dedicated-only steady-state (amortized committed capacity): ~$5.6 per 1M tokens (assumes commit for 4x A100 pool).
- Dedicated + caching/quantization (effective): ~$2.5 per 1M tokens (reduction mainly due to token efficiency and fewer re-computations).
- Hosted fallback (uncommitted autoscale): additional ~$9.1 per 1M tokens for traffic served on hosted multi-tenant pools.
- Mixed strategy (Dedicated handling 80% of burst, hosted fallback 20%): blended cost ~3.4 per 1M tokens for bursts.

Analysis and learnings:
1) Prefix/KV caching is the single most effective knob for this workload because rerank contexts re-use large prefixes. For customer workloads where prefix reuse < 40% the benefit drops off significantly.
2) Adaptive batching with a reasonably tight latency cap (100–150ms) allows high packing efficiency without pushing p95 beyond SLOs. Larger batch caps reduce cost further but hurt tail latency during bursts.
3) Pre-warm (cache population) and a short-lived warm reserve (extra Dedicated nodes that remain on hot for short windows) smooths microbursts without engaging hosted fallback for many real-world burst shapes.
4) Hosted fallback is expensive but necessary to guarantee availability for 6x microbursts unless the customer is willing to pay for substantial Dedicated overprovision.

Operational recommendations (customer-facing):
- Deployment shape: Dedicated pool of 4 x A100-80GB with the following runtime flags: prefix_cache=true, adaptive_batch_max=32, latency_cap_ms=120, kv_pre_warm=true.
- Autoscaling policy: aggressive scale-up (add 1 node) at sustained 65% GPU util for >30s, conservative scale-down only after util <50% for 300s to avoid oscillation during burst tails.
- Warm reserve plan: keep 0.5 node-equivalent warm buffer (pre-warmed storage) during known campaign windows; enabling dynamic warm reserve increases committed cost by ~8% but reduces fallback use by ~60%.
- Fallback routing: preferred-order policy -> Dedicated primary; regionally proximate hosted pool secondary; degrade to cheaper, lower-capacity model variant if both fail (redwood-mini-7b-quant) to preserve p95.

Runbook (play-by-play for an observed microburst):
1) Alerting: trigger when queue depth > 80 or p95 > 400ms for >60s.
2) Automated actions (via Console): spin up +1 Dedicated node; set routing to preferentially pack similar prefixes; enable short-lived higher batch cap for 60s.
3) If queue depth remains >120 after 90s, engage hosted fallback for overflow and notify SRE and customer ops.
4) Post-burst: mark which prefixes were cold, schedule pre-warm job (sample 10k historical prefixes) to replenish caches overnight.

Open questions and next experiments:
- Quantize-to-3bit experiment: evaluate if 3-bit runs maintain quality for rerank logits; expected to reduce token cost further but may require new kernel paths. Ticket created: OPS-4879.
- Longer burst shapes: we tested 3-minute sustained bursts; run a 30-minute campaign-shaped burst test with realistic inter-arrival distributions to validate scale-down policy.
- Multi-region failover latency: test cross-region fallback in APAC/NA to quantify cross-region p95 for fallback path.

Notes to customer (plain language):
- Recommendation is to proceed with a Dedicated pool sized for 4x steady-state with the runtime flags above and accept a small warm-reserve commit. This keeps unit cost low and p95 within SLO for most bursts; hosted fallback is kept as last-resort for disastrous spikes.
- We can run a 30-day pilot with metrics dashboarding (per-route p95, fallback ratio, committed cost burn) to validate economics in production traffic.

Appendix (raw numbers table snapshot):
- 1x steady: qps 220 | p95 340ms | GPU util 62% | cost est 5.6/1M tokens
- 4x burst no-cache: qps 720 | p95 1.2s | GPU util 98% | fallback 0% (latency degraded)
- 4x burst with cache+batch: qps 680 | p95 380ms | GPU util 88% | fallback 0%
- 6x burst mixed: qps 1320 | p95 combined 420ms | fallback share 16% | blended cost 3.4/1M tokens

Next steps (action items):
- [SE] Finalize runbook and push console automation playbooks (owner: Ethan Park) by 2027-11-22.
- [SRE] Schedule 30-minute campaign-shaped burst test and coordinate with Phoenix ops for traffic window (owner: Lucia Moreno) target 2027-11-29.
- [Research] Start 3-bit quantization quality evaluation on in-house rerank dataset (owner: Dmitri Kozlov) due 2027-12-06.

Document history:
- 2027-11-15 initial test notes (Aisha)
- 2027-11-17 added cost projections and runbook (Ethan)
- 2027-11-18 feedback incorporated from customer call; status set to draft pending pilot acceptance.

Unresolved items for customer call:
- Acceptable fallback cost band? Phoenix ops requested that fallback costs not exceed 2x of committed marginal cost during campaign windows. This constraint will likely require a larger warm reserve.
- SLO enforcement: customer asked whether automatic degrade to 7b variant should happen before fallback; team to propose exact latency thresholds.

End of document.
